question: What is a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: An abnormal tract connecting the rectum and vagina
options.B: A complete rupture of the perineal body muscles
options.C: A prolapse of the uterine wall into the rectum
options.D: An infection of the Bartholin gland

explanation: A rectovaginal fistula creates an unwanted passage allowing bowel contents to enter the vaginal canal. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: Why is a rectovaginal fistula often psychologically distressing for a patient?

options.A: It causes continuous involuntary passage of gas and stool vaginally
options.B: It prevents the patient from ever walking again
options.C: It causes severe upper abdominal pain after meals
options.D: It immediately leads to total kidney failure

explanation: The uncontrollable leakage of feces and flatus through the vagina causes significant hygiene challenges and social embarrassment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: What structure is compromised when a rectovaginal fistula forms?
explanation: The fistula forms when the partition or septum separating the rectum and vagina is damaged or breached. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: Why do established rectovaginal fistulas rarely heal on their own?

options.A: The tract becomes lined with epithelium
options.B: Bowel movements constantly stretch the perineum
options.C: Vaginal acidity dissolves new tissue growth
options.D: Continuous high blood pressure prevents clotting

explanation: Once epithelial tissue lines the abnormal passage, the body treats the tract as a normal surface, preventing natural closure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: What is the most common cause of rectovaginal fistula in developing countries?
explanation: Prolonged pressure from the baby's head against the pelvis causes tissue ischemia and necrosis, leading to fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of rectovaginal fistula?

options.B: Normal spontaneous vaginal delivery without tears

explanation: An uncomplicated, normal delivery does not cause the severe tissue damage necessary to create a rectovaginal fistula. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: What is the classic symptom reported by a patient with a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: Inability to empty the bladder completely
options.C: Passage of gas or stool through the vagina
options.D: Continuous watery discharge from the urethra

explanation: Because of the abnormal opening, bowel contents escape through the vaginal canal instead of the anus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h4)

question: A patient presents to the clinic reporting stool coming through her vagina two weeks after a difficult childbirth. What is the nurse's priority action during assessment?

options.A: Tell the patient this is a normal postpartum change that will resolve in a few days
options.B: Provide a gentle, empathetic history and prepare the patient for a careful physical examination
options.C: Perform a high-pressure enema to clear the bowel immediately
options.D: Immediately schedule the patient for emergency major surgery without further assessment

explanation: A sensitive history and gentle physical examination are essential to confirm the diagnosis and assess tissue health before planning treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h4)

question: Which diagnostic test involves placing dye in the rectum to see if it stains a vaginal gauze?
explanation: The methylene blue test helps confirm the presence of a tract by tracking fluid movement from the rectum into the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h5)

question: Why might an MRI or ultrasound be ordered for a patient with a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: To check for active urinary tract infections
options.B: To test the patient's liver enzymes and kidney function
options.C: To evaluate the condition of the sphincter muscles and surrounding deep tissues
options.D: To measure the patient's daily fluid intake and output

explanation: Advanced imaging helps surgeons see the exact path of the fistula and check if the anal sphincter muscles are also injured. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of bowel preparation before rectovaginal fistula surgery?

options.A: To reduce fecal load and minimize infection risk
options.B: To increase blood pressure during the operation
options.C: To stretch the vaginal walls for easier access
options.D: To test the kidneys for dye clearance

explanation: Clearing the bowel reduces stool contamination at the surgical site, lowering the risk of postoperative wound infection and failure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: How should a nurse address the psychological needs of a patient preparing for fistula repair?

options.A: Focus only on physical care because emotional feelings do not affect healing
options.B: Tell the patient that her condition is very rare and difficult to cure
options.C: Provide compassionate, non-judgmental support and explain all procedures clearly
options.D: Avoid talking about the condition to prevent embarrassing the patient

explanation: Patients suffer from heavy emotional distress and isolation, making empathetic communication and reassurance a vital part of nursing care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: What surgical approach accesses the fistula tract through the vaginal wall?
explanation: The transvaginal approach directly exposes and closes the defect through the posterior wall of the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h7)

question: Why might a surgeon sometimes create a temporary diverting colostomy during a fistula repair?

options.A: To make vaginal examinations easier for the nurse
options.B: To permanently replace the function of the rectum
options.C: To divert stool away from the healing surgical site
options.D: To allow the patient to eat solid food immediately after surgery

explanation: Diverting feces away from the repaired area protects the fresh sutures from contamination and promotes successful healing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h7)

question: Why are stool softeners commonly prescribed after rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: To increase the speed of food digestion in the stomach
options.B: To prevent straining that can disrupt the suture line
options.C: To increase blood flow to the lower limbs
options.D: To cure chronic urinary tract infections

explanation: Avoiding hard stools and straining protects the delicate surgical repairs from tension and tearing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: A postoperative patient asks to have her temperature taken rectally. What is the correct nursing response?

options.A: Refuse to check her temperature at all during the entire hospital stay
options.B: Perform the rectal temperature quickly and gently with lots of lubrication
options.C: Ask the patient to insert the thermometer herself to avoid causing pain
options.D: Explain that rectal temperatures are contraindicated to protect the surgical repair

explanation: Any instrument placed in the rectum can damage the fresh surgical repair site and cause the surgery to fail. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: What is a common potential complication following rectovaginal fistula repair?
explanation: Due to tension, infection, or poor tissue healing, the fistula can sometimes reopen, requiring further medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h9)

question: What is the purpose of recommending pelvic floor exercises in the long-term recovery phase?

options.A: To help restore and strengthen anal sphincter tone
options.B: To speed up the healing of abdominal skin scars
options.C: To increase the production of digestive enzymes
options.D: To prevent the development of high blood pressure

explanation: Strengthening the pelvic floor muscles improves overall continence and pelvic support after surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h9)
